rulings.failure_scenario: A maintainer reads a PASS on the changelog surface and believes the v0.6.0 entry's four README.md claims were compared against README.md, when no byte of README.md was in this bundle, so a "Fixed" bullet describing a README repair that never landed would have been reported by nobody.
rulings.reason: This is a gap in the gate's own coverage, not a defect in the release. The changelog surface is asked whether this entry's claims are true, and four of them are about README.md, which surfaces.yaml does not hand it — so the agent reported the byte it needed rather than guessing, which is what the frame asks for. The risk it names is real in general: a Fixed bullet describing a README repair that never landed would go unreported by this surface. It has not materialised here. All four claims were checked before this ruling was written, each by a test that EXECUTES the documented procedure rather than reading it: TestPasteBlockYesToHookStillEndsWithCI and its No sibling, TestPasteBlockExportRunsRootedAndTeachesTheHarness, TestREADME_DigestStoreCommitTimingMatchesTheEngine, and TestPreLedgerCrossing. All pass against this tree. The durable fix is a reads: entry for README.md on the changelog surface; it is not taken now because the edit would move the tree and cost a full thirteen-agent round to re-earn a receipt this release already holds, for a gap that verifiably cost nothing this time. It is owed to the next release, and this ruling is the record of the debt.
